item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.
After the follow-up, the final result is widescreen 16:9 (the user changed the shape from vertical 9:16); everything else is as before.

changed_by.say: actually, make it widescreen instead of vertical and keep everything else the same.

args.name: Why We Hear Echoes — Kids Explainer

style.prompt: Create a 10-second vertical educational explainer for young kids, with generated English voice-over. Bright friendly 2D cartoon, colorful clean shapes, clear visual teaching, no live action. A cute small orange cartoon fox stands on the left in a grassy valley, facing a large flat cliff on the right. Use a single steady wide composition with both fox and cliff visible. At the start the fox makes a little call. Animate a few clearly visible blue curved sound-wave arcs traveling from the fox to the cliff, reflecting at the cliff, then returning toward the fox's ears. The returning arcs should clearly demonstrate reflection, not a second sound source. End with the fox smiling and listening, one paw beside its ear. Cheerful sky and soft rounded landscape, high contrast sound waves, uncluttered mobile-friendly composition. A friendly warm narrator speaks this exact script clearly across the ten seconds: 'Why do we hear echoes? Sound travels in waves. When waves bounce off something far away and come back, we hear the sound again!' Voice-over is the primary audio, natural friendly delivery, no music overpowering it, fox does not lip sync the narration. No additional spoken words. No text required. Scientifically show sound traveling outward, bouncing off a distant hard surface, and returning with a delay.
